old_problem: The active review correctly gated execution but bundled the missing OEM command meaning with ordinary runtime parameters. No public Linux, AMD, IPMI or Redfish authority defines `/tmp/gpu_caution1` as a Wistron BMC thermal-injection interface, so its controller namespace, firmware applicability, response and cleanup cannot be inferred.
disposition_reason: This is a private OEM control-plane interface, not a standard filesystem or IPMI command. ED-03 permits a draft but prohibits guessing OEM parameters; ED-09 keeps BMC-console and physical fan observation manual; ED-16 requires an approved injection mechanism and recovery; ED-17 requires preserving SEL evidence. A mere successful `touch` only proves file creation and cannot authorize or prove a synthetic 101 C event. The case remains pending until the exact firmware-scoped interface and recovery are supplied.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row413 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3005, same-code row148 and adjacent row414 caution2 case.
Separated same-code row148 TransferBench coverage from this OEM thermal-caution injection per ED-02/ED-19.
Confirmed that standard Linux file creation, IPMI sensor access and Redfish telemetry do not define this private marker's injection semantics.
Preserved the non-heating 101 C, critical event, full-fan and marker-removal intent while rejecting SSH password automation and log clearing.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row414 and verified its manifest identity; no marker, fan action or DUT/BMC command ran.

test_case.test_name: OEM-approved caution1 synthetic 101 C alert and full-fan recovery
test_case.purpose: Using only the firmware-approved non-heating caution1 interface, prove the mapped GPU sensor reports 101 C, emits the required temporary critical evidence, drives fans to full speed and returns to normal after cleanup.
required_package: Wistron-controlled specification naming the supported BMC/firmware build, controller namespace, exact marker path/owner/mode and caution1 state-machine semantics
Approved sensor ID/value/tolerance, SEL and host-log event IDs/text, fan-zone/PWM/RPM response and latency/dwell limits
Qualified BMC-console operator, stable BMC/host time correlation, independent fan/RPM or physical observation and OOB access
Mandatory marker-removal verification, latch-clear procedure, abort conditions and recovery owner
test_case.test_command: PENDING OEM AUTHORITY. After written approval, preserve BMC SDR/SEL, host dmesg and fan-zone/RPM baselines. A qualified operator at the specified BMC console creates exactly the approved caution1 marker once. Independently timestamp the mapped sensor reaching 101 C within tolerance, required temporary critical SEL/host event and full-fan PWM/RPM plus physical evidence. Remove the marker within the approved dwell and verify marker absence, sensor normalization, alert transition and fan recovery.
test_case.expected_result: Only the approved synthetic sensor enters the documented 101 C caution state; the exact critical events appear and the correct fan zones reach approved full-speed evidence. After marker removal, the injected state clears within the specified time, normal fan policy resumes and no real overtemperature, unintended shutdown, device loss or residual latch remains.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PENDING: PASS is forbidden until the OEM specification defines the exact interface, sensor/event/fan oracle and cleanup. After approval, all before/during/after artifacts, manual fan proof and recovery must match that specification; file existence or a truncated log tail alone cannot pass.
safety_gate: Prove the marker is a supported non-heating injection for the exact BMC firmware; do not discover semantics on a DUT
Use the approved BMC console and qualified operator only; do not embed credentials or automate the physical observation
Preserve SEL/dmesg before injection and maintain independent management and a strict dwell/removal timer
Abort and remove the marker on wrong sensor/event/fan response, real thermal/power anomaly, access loss or unexpected shutdown; never auto-retry
expected_evidence: Signed OEM marker/controller/firmware specification and approval
Before/during/after marker state, SDR sensor identity/value and complete SEL/dmesg event evidence
Fan-zone command/PWM/RPM telemetry plus timestamped manual visual or acoustic evidence
Marker removal, normalized sensor/fan/event state and full BMC/host/GPU post-health
test_case.recovery: Remove the marker through the OEM-approved console, verify its absence and injected-state clear, preserve all evidence, and follow the documented BMC service or controlled power recovery only if the state remains latched. Do not clear SEL, reboot, power-cycle or retry unless the signed recovery procedure authorizes that step.
